title: Costume State / Identity Migrates Through Wear

source_refs.author: Costume design and performance analysis
source_refs.title: Wardrobe state as continuity and identity evidence

observed_structure: a garment establishes role, status, or public identity
ownership, wear, damage, or arrangement changes
the altered costume state changes behavior or social recognition
dramatic_operations: record role change in material state
separate public mask from operative self
cinematic_affordances: same garment worn by a different person
fastening, removal, damage, or repair emphasized
social reaction changing before verbal recognition
cultural_scope: costume meaning is project- and culture-specific; avoid universalizing colors, garments, or dress codes
misuse_risks: costume change as shorthand without behavior change
cultural clothing used as archetype costume
transferable_structure: a change in garment ownership or material state makes a role transition legible and alters subsequent behavior
non_transferable_surface: specific uniforms, ceremonial dress, or culturally coded clothing used without contextual provenance
